en: Before becoming a national hero, Jose Rizal secretly performed an eye surgery on his mother to cure her cataracts.
The Philippine national flag is the only flag in the world that is flown upside down to indicate a state of war.
T'boli women weave the intricate T'nalak cloth using complex, sacred patterns that they see in their dreams.
Doctor Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift bamboo incubator with hot water bottles to help premature babies in rural areas.
The original Bayanihan tradition involved an entire community physically carrying a heavy, traditional nipa hut on their shoulders to relocate it.
Dancers in the Ati-Atihan festival paint their bodies with black soot to honor and imitate the indigenous Ati people.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct living languages, making it one of the most linguistically diverse countries on Earth.
The Philippine Senate is composed of exactly twenty-four senators who are elected at large by voters from the entire country.
Marcela Agoncillo and her two daughters sewed the first official Philippine flag in Hong Kong before it was raised in Kawit.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo pioneered a unique backlighting technique to paint the glowing, golden sunlight in his rural Philippine scenes.
Under Philippine law, the Sandiganbayan is a special court dedicated exclusively to trying and punishing corrupt government officials.
The South Sea Pearl, harvested from the deep waters of Palawan, is the official national gem of the Philippines.
